hints.content:
###The strategy

$\text{Area of a rectangle} = \text{base} \cdot \text{height}$

Before we can apply the formula to find the area of rectangle $ABCD$, we must find the base and height of the rectangle using the Pythagorean theorem (or the distance formula).

* The base is the length $AB$.
* The height is the length $BC$.

###Step 1: Find the length $AB$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
AB^2&= {\redE{12}^2 +\redE{4}^2 }  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
AB&= \sqrt{\redE{12}^2 +\redE{4}^2 }  &&\text{Square root both sides}\\\\
&=\sqrt{160} \\\\
&=\sqrt{16\cdot10} \\\\
&=\tealE{4\sqrt{10}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Rectangle A B C D has point A at negative six, negative six, point B at six, negative two, point C at four, four and point D at negative eight, zero. A horizontal line of twelve units connects from point A to a vertical line of four units connecting to point B.

hints.content:
###Step 2: Find the length $BC$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
BC^2&= \redE{2}^2 +\redE{6}^2  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
BC&= \sqrt{\redE{2}^2 +\redE{6}^2 } &&\text{Square root both sides} \\\\
&=\sqrt{40} \\\\
&=\sqrt{4 \cdot 10} \\\\
&=\goldE{2\sqrt{10}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Rectangle A B C D has point A at negative six, negative six, point B at six, negative two, point C at four, four and point D at negative eight, zero. A horizontal line of two units connects from point C to a vertical line of six units connecting to point B.

hints.content:
###Step 3: Find the area of the rectangle

Using the base and height of rectangle $ABCD$, we can find the area:

$\begin{align} \text{Area of a rectangle} &= \text{base} \cdot \text{height}\\\\
&= AB \cdot BC \\\\
&= (\tealE{4\sqrt{10}})\cdot(\goldE{2\sqrt{10}}) \\\\
&= 8\cdot\sqrt{10}\cdot\sqrt{10} \\\\
&= 8\cdot10 \\\\
&= 80
\end{align}$

###The answer:

The area of rectangle $ABCD$ is $80$ units$^2$.

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
Yes, we can find the area of the outer rectangle, then subtract the areas of the triangular regions outside of rectangle $ABCD$.



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_{ABCD} &= 14(10) - \text{Area}_{\triangle1} - \text{Area}_{\triangle2} - \text{Area}_{\triangle3} - \text{Area}_{\triangle4} \\\\
&=140 - \dfrac{1}{2}(12)(4)-\dfrac{1}{2}(2)(6)- \dfrac{1}{2}(12)(4)-\dfrac{1}{2}(2)(6)\\\\
&=140-24-6-24-6\\\\
&=80
\end{align}$

The area of rectangle $ABCD$ is $80$ units$^2$.
options.showPrompt: Could we find the area another way?

options.alt: A coordinate plane.  Rectangle A B C D has point A at negative six, negative six, point B at six, negative two, point C at four, four and point D at negative eight, zero. Rectangle A B C D is inscribed in another rectangle that has a point at negative eight, negative six, a point at six, negative six, a point at six, four, and a point at negative eight, four. This creates four triangles that are cut out of the larger rectangle by rectangle A B C D. The bottom right triangle is triangle one. The top right triangle is triangle two. The top left triangle is triangle three. The bottom left triangle is triangle four.
